question.leadin: Following the failure of the Shimabara Rebellion during this period, Christians were forced underground.
question.text: Name this last shogunate [show-gun-ate] of Japan. Commodore Matthew Perry entered Japan while this shogunate was in power.
question.clue: Inspectors called metsuke battled corruption during this period, during which local lords were forced to rotate residency between home and the capital in the sankin-kotai system.

swap.text: Much later in the war, American forces placed a flag on Mount Suribachi during a battle on this small Japanese island.
swap.clue: The last American carrier lost in the war, the USSBismarck Sea, was lost at the battle to capturethisJapanese island. The fighting was immortalized by photographer Joe Rosenthal on Mount Suribachi.

question.leadin: Give the following about earthquakes that have devastated Japan.
question.text: Both the 2011 and 1923 earthquakes were centered near this largest Japanese island.
question.clue: By far the largest of the four main islands is this one, home to Tokyo, Kyoto, and Nagoya.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
swap.text: This victor of Sekigahara created that new shogunate and moved the capital from Kyoto to Edo, soon renamed Tokyo. His line would rule as shogun until the Meiji Restoration
swap.clue: After being designated Hideyori's regent, he defeated Ishida Mitsunari's Eastern Army at Sekigahara.

question.leadin: This man survived an assassination attempt by Lee Bong Chang, known as the Sakuradamon Incident.
question.text: Name this emperor of Japan during World War II, who implored his people to "endure the unendurable" before surrendering.
question.clue: This leader's Prime Minister was killed by the League of Blood in the May 15th Incident.

swap.text: This was the first city ever to be hit by a nuclear bomb. The B-29 Enola Gay was responsible for the dropping of the uranium "Little Boy" bomb on this Japanese city.
swap.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

question.leadin: Manchuria was given back to China through the terms of this treaty.
question.text: Identify this agreement which saw one side gain control of half of Sakhalin Island.
question.clue: For brokering this treaty, which the parties signed in Kittery, Maine, U.S. president Theodore Roosevelt received the Nobel Peace Prize.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the life of Julia Ota, a young prisoner of war from 16th century Korea.
swap.text: Julia was adopted by Konishi Yukinaga, a leading general during this leader's late-1500s invasion of Korea.
swap.clue: He codified laws that crystallized the hierarchy of samurai, peasant, artisan, and merchant as well as ordering the 1588 Great Sword Hunt, ostensibly to decorate a temple enshrining himself.

question.text: This first shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was dominated by the Hojo family.
question.clue: The Jokyu incident, an early attempt to end its rule, was led by Go-Toba and was defeated at the Third Battle of Uji by the Hojo clan, who served as the true rulers following the death of Minamoto.

swap.text: This emperor gave the Jewel Voice Broadcast announcing that Japan had surrendered in World War II.
swap.clue: The empowerment of this man was the state goal of the League of Blood, while the year of his ascension saw a financial crisis triggered by the devaluation of Earthquake Bonds, leading to the rise of conglomerate control of the economy.

question.leadin: This conflict was the boiling over of a dispute between the "Red Monk," Yamana Sozen, and his rival and son-in-law, Hosokawa Katsumoto.
question.text: Name this succession crisis in fifteenth-century Japan that began with the death of emperor Yoshimasa.
question.clue: As a result of this conflict, the Hosokawa Clan became de-facto rulers of Japan.

swap.text: This city near the Kyoto-Kobe-Osaka metropolis contains lots of tame deer that roam around its many temples. Todai-ji, 7 other temples, and a forest make up the UNESCO World Heritage site of this city.
swap.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

question.text: In correspondence with Emperor Yang of Sui, this prince encouraged him to call Japan by Nihon. Through the Seventeen-Article Constitution, he promoted Buddhism as Japan's state religion.

swap.leadin: The Beipu uprising, an early uprising against this colonial power, was joined by many members of the Saisiyat tribe.
swap.text: Name this colonial power, which fought the Truku War with local aboriginals. Mona Rudao was a leader of the Seediq people that fought against this colonial power in the Musha Incident.
swap.clue: Its navy staged a successful attack in the Battle of Port Arthur during a conflict ended by negotiations in Maine with a rival country's diplomat Sergei Witte.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese naval battles.
question.text: Taguchi Shigeyoshi's defection from the Taira helped Minamoto Yoshitsune lead his fleet to victory in this 1185 battle which effectively ended the Gempei War and cleared the way for founding of the Kamakura shogunate.
question.clue: This battle saw Taguchi Shigeyoshi reveal the location of the Emperor's ship, and both the child-emperor Antoku and his grandmother, the widow of Kiyomori, committed suicide.

swap.leadin: This text, whose name is sometimes translated as "Chronicles of Japan," is the second-oldest extant piece of Japanese literature after the Kojiki.
swap.text: Name this set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.
swap.clue: This historical work claims that Emperor Tenmu played sugoroku, a backgammon-like game that was later banned due to its players' propensity for gambling. Unlike the Kojiki, this work of history extends until the 8th century.

question.leadin: The Mitchell Monument in Bly, Oregon commemorates six civilian deaths that occurred as a result of one of these weapons.
question.text: Name these weapons, over 9000 of which were launched by the Japanese army in the closing years of World War II, known as Operation Fu-Go.
question.answerHtml: balloon bombs [or incendiary balloons; or fire balloons; accept answers describing explosive balloons; accept Fu-Go balloon bombs; prompt on balloons; prompt on bombs or explosives or incendiaries]

swap.leadin: Workers for this center referred to their test subjects as "logs" because the official cover for their activities was that they were a forestry research station.
swap.text: Commanded by Shiro Ishii, name this experimental research station in Manchuria that used captured prisoners and local Chinese for experiments on the bubonic plague, freezing, vivisection, and suffocation.
swap.clue: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.

question.text: The story is often backdated to apply to the rule of this man, who became the first shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate after he'd originally allied with Go-Daigo whom he later turned against.
question.clue: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

swap.leadin: You are a Tokugawa official tasked with uncovering Kakure Kirishitan, or hidden Christians. You also have a terrible secret of your own: you are Auroni Gupta.
swap.text: You hope no one notices your UCSD sweatshirt under your kimono as you try to identify Kirishitan by seeing who refuses to step on these flat images of Christian symbols, whose name literally means "stepping- on pictures."
swap.clue: Under the Tokugawa shogunate, Nagasaki Christians were often required to step on these depictions of Jesus or the Virgin Mary, at the risk of torture. These objects were usually made from bronze or painted stone.
